advice:
# Lava Tactics: the game plan

Approved by the user on 2026-10-14 (B186). Every worker reads it; parts 1 to 4 change only with the user's yes. The
answers it is built on: [the Advisor's decisions](lava-tactics/docs/advisor/decisions.md). The old roadmap:
[archived](lava-tactics/docs/archive/roadmap-2026-10.md).

## 1. The goal

A growing roguelite later; first a polished game with what exists.

- **Horizon:** new worlds, units, heroes, skills, upgrades, levels, and resources to spend.
- **Now:** World 1, the Knight and the Wizard, today's enemies, the upgrades and the run, polished.
- **Beside it:** the worker board gets faster and usable for any project.
- **Built to scale:** every kind of content is data, and the code is built for that.

## 2. Milestones

M1 the loop is fun → M2 version 1, polished → M3 and on, growth.

| Milestone | What you get | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| **M1 · The loop is fun** | a World 1 run of 5 fights, each bringing one new trouble; heroes who start with two abilities and grow by upgrades; three new enemies; the polish to judge fun; your experiments | 2 whole runs played, you say "fun", no bug breaks a run |
| **M2 · Version 1, polished** | the reference look on every map; start screen, run summary and settings finished; a shop that sells; sound for every moment; the rest of the 4x art; no known bugs | someone else plays it start to end in the browser without help |
| **M3+ · Growth** | worlds, units, heroes, skills, upgrades, levels, resources: one milestone each | picked after M2 |

- **M1's strategy** (your brainstorm of 2026-10-18, about 19 h): each hero starts a run with two abilities; after
  every won fight you pick 1 of 3 upgrades drawn across both heroes (2 after a fight with elites), to unlock an
  ability, improve one, or learn a new one (Knight: Charge, Iron Skin, Shield Throw; Wizard: Stone Wall, Slow Ground,
  Blink); Bats, the Ballista and the Brute join today's four enemies, one new trouble per fight. It replaced R4.
- **M1's polish:** damage and push shown before a click; hits, pushes and deaths with effects and sound; a readable
  upgrade offer and run map; nothing drawn in the wrong order.
- **M1's experiments, each behind a setting:** undo an action or a turn; enemies that show their next move (B07),
  and other ways to show it; cascading effects with the whole outcome shown before the click. M1 can be finished
  without them (your yes to B278, 2026-10-17: enemy intent moved here from M1's must-haves).
- **M1's maps** (your brainstorms of 2026-10-18 and 2026-10-19): better maps (G23), where you see at once where to
  walk and where a push kills, and interesting level design (G28, about 26 h): eight ideas painted with Codex, built
  as three set-piece shapes, ground that changes during a fight, objectives beyond killing everyone and
  reinforcements shown a turn ahead (G29 to G32). M1 can be finished without them: your two runs (R6) may come first.
- The way to M1, step by step: the board's "Next milestone" part.
- **The first growth milestone after M2 is World 2** (your yes to B45, 2026-10-19): the Ashen Reach already stands
  in the data with World 1's content filling in, and a run goes on into it after the Lava Golem; its own brainstorm
  comes right after M2.

## 3. Foundations

What must exist before the second of each kind. ✅ there · ⏳ still to build, and when.

| Kind | Foundation | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Units' art | definition of done, prompt kit, line-up of all units, walk views in four directions | ✅ |
| Enemies | intent, and behaviour as data | ⏳ intent with its experiment (B07); behaviour as data before M3 (B366) |
| Outcome preview | an action's or an enemy turn's result shown before it happens | ✅ an action's result (B304, B306) · ⏳ an enemy turn's with its experiment |
| Heroes | a hero as data that owns its abilities and stats | ✅ its abilities carried through a run (B309) · ⏳ its stats before M3 (B367) |
| Abilities | effects, visuals and sounds as data | ⏳ before M3 (B365) |
| Upgrades | an upgrade's changes as data | ✅ "an ability does more" · ✅ unlock an ability and a trait (B310, B312) · ⏳ other kinds before M3 |
| Battlefield | a map that changes during a fight: a rock or slow tiles for some turns | ✅ built (B313), its preview fix in review (B370) |
| Level rules | objectives, changing ground and reinforcements as data, so World 2 reuses them | ⏳ with G30 to G32 |
| Maps and worlds | definition of done and playbook; a world is one data entry | ✅ |
| Ground's look | a standard against the reference pictures | ✅ [the definition of done](process/done/ground-look.md) (B355) · ⏳ the look itself (B308) |
| Safety nets | test battles and screenshot checks | ✅ a bot plays every path of a run (B303) · ⏳ screenshot checks before M2's polish (B09) |
| Screens, props, sound | definitions of done and playbooks | ✅ |

## 4. How you work

Prototype fast on a solid base, and clean up as you go.

- **Solid from the start:** the game rules and their tests, the content formats, the foundations above.
- **Rough first, polished in M2:** the ground's look, the start screen, settings, the shop.
- **New content is tried rough:** quick art first; full art (target 75) once you keep it. A unit's quick art is
  still its full set of animations (idle, attack, hit, death, its walks), only rougher; a unit without them does not
  merge (B283: the Lava Golem came as one still picture).
- **Experiments go behind a setting;** the variant that loses is removed.
- **Clean-up:** a branch and a folder per task, gone at its merge; unused code, art and sounds go after your yes
  (the Advisor's weekly round).
- **Before work:** a big step, or the first or second of a kind, is checked with the Advisor; a feature that reaches
  into the game's structure gets a warning first, with the course the Advisor advises.
- **After work (your Go on G11, 2026-10-18):** nothing is done unchecked. Every kind of produced thing (a unit, a map, a
  screen, a prop, a sound, a skill effect, the ground's look, a HUD piece) has its definition of done and its reference
  before it is built, named in its refined step. A step is done only when a helper that did not build it ticked every
  agreed point against them, with the result beside its reference at play size; a failed point makes a fix step by
  itself. A goal is ticked only after a re-check against its "Done when". You get a recap with the picture, which
  approves itself unless you overturn it. After three failed attempts on one goal, a fundamental evaluation in high
  effort mode asks whether the approach is right; a rebuild needs your yes unless you set the board to approve it by
  itself. (The board builds it: B353 to B361.)
